description: 6 should-trigger + 7 should-not-trigger. Should-trigger covers job-shape to provider matching, including the two rows the vector split changed: an icon routing question whose routed answer is now no provider, and complex illustrative vector art, the one shape a vector provider still owns. Should-not-trigger covers near-miss neighbors: writing the actual prompt (prompt-engineering-image), invoking the adapter directly, media policy checks (media-governance-routing), general image editing without a routing question, and the two hand-authoring requests that go to svg-authoring rather than to any provider.

queries.q: which image model should I use for a logo with text?
route this image generation job — it needs a photorealistic product shot
I need a vector SVG icon, what provider handles that?
queries.note: still a routing question, and after the vector split the routed answer is NO provider — the incumbent set first, then svg-authoring for a glyph it lacks

queries.q: which provider do I use for complex illustrative vector art?
queries.note: the one job shape a vector provider still owns; the answer states the adapter scaffold-tier lifecycle

queries.q: pick the right AI image provider for a bakery banner with the name on it
should I use Ideogram or Flux for this image brief?
write me an Ideogram prompt for this logo brief
run the recraft adapter with this prompt
queries.note: direct adapter invocation, not routing selection

queries.q: can I use a celebrity's face in this image?
edit this existing photo to remove the background
queries.note: editing task, not a provider routing decision

queries.q: what lifecycle tier is the Flux adapter?
draw an SVG icon our set does not have — a split-branch glyph
queries.note: hand-authoring, not provider selection → iconography then svg-authoring

queries.q: author a simple geometric mark as SVG — two overlapping circles
queries.note: hand-authored mark → svg-authoring; no provider is involved
